chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, he said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said:

When the Qa'im arises, he will send out into the regions of the earth, to every region a man, saying: 'Your covenant is in your hand.' So when a matter comes to you that you do not understand and do not know the judgment for, look at your hand and act according to what is in it.' He said: 'And he will send an army to Constantinople. When they reach the sea, they will write something on their feet and walk on the water. When the Romans see them walking on the water, they will say: 'These are his companions walking on the water, so how is he (the Imam)?' At that, they will open the gates of the city for them, they will enter it, and rule in it as they wish.

key_terms.أَقَالِيمِ الْأَرْضِ: Regions of the earth, referring to the global distribution of his delegates
key_terms.الرُّومُ: The Romans (Byzantines), the opposing force in this eschatological narrative
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ: Constantinople, the city targeted for conquest
key_terms.عَهْدُكَ: Your covenant, referring to a token or document carried by the delegate

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and actions of al-Qa'im regarding governance and the conquest of Constantinople?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration highlights the decentralized yet unified administrative structure of the Mahdi’s era, where regional delegates hold a 'covenant' (‘ahd) in hand to resolve ambiguous matters, reflecting the Shia concept of general deputies during the Major Occultation. The miraculous crossing of the Romans (Byzantines) to Constantinople serves as a divine sign of legitimacy, echoing the historical expectation of the conquest of the two Romes and fulfilling the promise of ultimate authority over the earth.
